messages.author: 6bc640c9f98380b3
messages.subject: regmatches
parts:
I've been meaning for some time to alert subscribers to the list to a change in R 2.14 (and so not reflected in QCLWR which was pre-R 2.14). The function regmatches() has been available since R 2.14 to return the exact matches from a gregexpr() pattern search:

> vector1 = c("This a string.", "This is another.")
> positions.lengths = gregexpr("\\w+", vector1, perl = TRUE)
> matches = regmatches(vector1, positions.lengths)
> matches

[[1]]

[1] "This"   "a"      "string"

[[2]]

[1] "This"    "is"      "another"

> unlist(matches)

[1] "This"    "a"       "string"  "This"    "is"      "another"

Obviously regmatches() doesn't do as much as Stefan's exact.matches(), but it is a way to get matches to a pattern from the base package of R.

John

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: regmatches
parts:
Talking about benchmarking exact.matches() (in another thread), it is interesting to see that exact.matches()[[1]] is twice as fast as regmatches(). I would have thought that regmatches(), being included in the base package now, would be faster than exact.matches()[[1]], but that doesn't seem to be the case. Take a look:

> aa<-c("some sentence here, whatever it may be", "and another one here too")
> aa<-rep(aa, 50000)
> search.term<-"here"
>
> system.time({
+     bb<-gregexpr(search.term, aa, perl=T)
+     cc<-unlist(regmatches(aa, bb))
+ })
   user  system elapsed
  1.509   0.109   1.613
>
> source("http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries/exact_matches.r")
> system.time({
+     dd<-exact.matches(search.term, aa)[[1]]
+ })
   user  system elapsed
  0.786   0.071   0.851
>
> identical(cc, dd)
[1] TRUE

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: regmatches
parts:
Has anyone found a way to do multiple string captures with a regex with base R, like what can be done with:

stringr::str_match_all

I want to use a regex to capture both the links as well as the hyperlink text in the HTML source of a webpage. For example:

webpage <- 'some webpage with whatever content with a <a href="http://domain.org/specific_webpage">link</a> and another one <a href="http://domain.org/another_page">here</a>'

library("stringr")

matches <- str_match_all(webpage, regex("href=\"([^\"]+)\">([^<]+)"))
links <- matches[[1]][, 2]
hyperlink_text <- matches[[1]][, 3]

Using base::gsub only retrieves the first link and associated hyperlink text, rather than all of them:

temp <- gsub("^.*?href=\"([^\"]+)\">([^<]+).*?$", "\\1 \\2", webpage)
temp <- strsplit(temp, " ")
link <- temp[[1]][1]
hyperlink_text <- temp[[1]][2]

Thanks for any help,
Earl

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: regmatches

I haven't seen anything in base R, but

(i) do you mean something like this or am I not understanding you right?

webpage                                      %>%
   exact.matches("href=\"[^\"]+\">[^<]+", .) %>%
   "[["(1)                                   %>%
   gsub("(href=\")([^\"]+)(\">)([^<]+)",
        "\\2\t\\4",
        ., perl=TRUE)                        %>%
   strsplit("\t")

(ii) I do know that gsubfn::strapply and related functions can be useful for this, too:

strapplyc(webpage, "href=\"([^\"]+)\">([^<]+)")
# [[1]]
# [1] "http://domain.org/specific_webpage" "link"
# [3] "http://domain.org/another_page" "here"

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: regmatches
parts: I actually ended up using regmatches, as I don't need all of exact.matches' functionality:
webpage <- 'some webpage with whatever content with a <a href="http://domain.org/specific_webpage">link</a> and another one <a href="http://domain.org/another_page">here</a>'

temp <- gregexpr("href=\"[^\"]+\">[^<]+", webpage)
temp <- regmatches(webpage, temp)[[1]]
temp <- gsub("href=\"([^\"]+)\">([^<]+)", "\\1\t\\2", temp)
temp <- strsplit(temp, "\t")

links <- sapply(temp, function(x) x[1])
hyper_text <- sapply(temp, function(x) x[2])
